`Router.add` at `src/router.ts:42` is the SPI every router implements and the single entry point Hono uses to register routes, so a signature change fans out in four layers.

## 1. The five implementations (all break immediately)

| File | Line |
|---|---|
| `src/router/trie-router/router.ts` | 13 |
| `src/router/linear-router/router.ts` | 15 |
| `src/router/pattern-router/router.ts` | 10 — also self-recurses at `:17` for optional params |
| `src/router/reg-exp-router/router.ts` | 134 |
| `src/router/smart-router/router.ts` | 13 |

Each is `implements Router<T>`, so TS errors at the class declaration if the new signature isn't satisfied.

## 2. SmartRouter's replay buffer — the subtle one

`SmartRouter` records calls and replays them into whichever router wins:

- `routes?: [string, string, T][]` (`smart-router/router.ts:7`) is a hand-written mirror of the parameter list
- `add` pushes `[method, path, handler]` (`:18`)
- `match` replays via spread: `router.add(...args)` (`:34`)

The tuple type must change in lockstep. A **required** 4th parameter makes the spread a type error; an optional one type-checks but silently drops the new argument at replay time — a runtime bug that no compiler catches. This is the piece most likely to be missed.

## 3. Internal callers

- `src/hono-base.ts:381`, inside `private addRoute` — the sole funnel for `app.get/post/use/route/mount/on`, so every routing path in the framework goes through this one call.
- `src/middleware/combine/index.ts:139` — `except()` builds an ad-hoc `TrieRouter<true>` and calls `add(METHOD_NAME_ALL, condition, true)`.

## 4. Downstream storage (if you're adding data, not just renaming)

`TrieRouter.add` delegates to `Node.insert(method, path, handler)` (`trie-router/node.ts:38`); RegExpRouter stores `HandlerWithMetadata<T>` = `[handler, paramCount]`; Linear/Pattern push 3-tuples. Threading a new argument through means touching those too, plus `trie-router/node.test.ts` (~60 direct `insert` calls).

## 5. Tests and benchmarks

131 `.add(` call sites in `src/`, dominated by `src/router/common.case.test.ts` (92) — that suite runs against all four routers, so it breaks once and reports four times. Plus `reg-exp-router/router.test.ts` (20), `linear-router/router.test.ts` (5), `pattern-router/router.test.ts` (3). Outside `src/`: `benchmarks/routers/src/hono.mts`, `benchmarks/routers/src/bench-includes-init.mts:56,63,70,102`, `benchmarks/routers-deno/src/hono.mts`.

## 6. Public API — this is semver-breaking

`package.json` exports `./router` and each `./router/*` subpath, so `Router<T>` is a published interface. Third-party routers implementing it (a documented extension point) break on any added *required* parameter or any change to existing parameter types.

## Practical guidance

- **Adding an optional 4th param** (`add(method, path, handler, options?)`): non-breaking for external implementers (TS allows implementations with fewer params) and for callers. But you still must update `SmartRouter`'s tuple + spread or the option is silently lost after the router is chosen.
- **Narrowing existing types** (e.g. `method: string` → a `Method` union): breaks essentially every call site above, including the 131 test calls that pass string literals like `'PURGE'` (`common.case.test.ts:61`) and lowercase `'get'` (`:681`).
- **Changing return type** from `void`: `hono-base.ts:381` discards the result, and `SmartRouter`'s `forEach` replay discards it too.
